description: The bar chart illustrates the time distribution (in seconds) across three stages—Search, Extract, and Retrieval—for four performance metrics: Avg., 50%, 75%, and 90%—likely representing average, median, and percentile response times in the WebGLM system. The vertical axis ranges from 0.0 to 8.0 seconds with tick marks at 2.0-second intervals, while the horizontal axis lists the four metrics in increasing order of performance threshold. Each bar is a stacked composition of three colored segments: dark blue for Search, medium blue for Extract, and light blue for Retrieval, as indicated by the legend in the top-left corner. At the “Avg.” level, Search accounts for approximately 1.8 sec, Extract for ~2.2 sec, and Retrieval for ~1.0 sec, totaling ~5.0 sec. At “50%”, Search is ~1.5 sec, Extract ~1.8 sec, and Retrieval ~0.7 sec, summing to ~4.0 sec. At “75%”, Search is ~1.8 sec, Extract ~2.5 sec, and Retrieval ~0.8 sec, totaling ~5.1 sec. At “90%”, Search is ~2.0 sec, Extract ~4.8 sec, and Retrieval ~1.2 sec, summing to ~8.0 sec. The chart visually emphasizes that Extract dominates the time cost, especially at higher percentiles, while Retrieval remains relatively small across all metrics.
